title: The wrong order
setting: Lunch at a busy café in Jakarta. You ordered chicken fried rice, not spicy, and an iced tea. A young woman serving comes over with a plate.

n1.speaker: server
n1.indonesian: Permisi, Kak. Ini mi gorengnya, ya.
n1.english: Excuse me. Here are your fried noodles.

options.feedback: Maaf first keeps it polite, even though the mistake is theirs.

options.indonesian: Maaf, Mbak, saya pesan nasi goreng ayam, bukan mi goreng.
options.english: Sorry, I ordered chicken fried rice, not fried noodles.
options.feedback: Says what you ordered, so she can put it right straight away. Bukan contrasts the two dishes.
Tidak can't go before a noun. Pesanan (order) is a thing, so it's bukan: Ini bukan pesanan saya.

n2.speaker: server
n2.indonesian: Oh, maaf, Kak. Tadi pesan apa, ya?
n2.english: Oh, sorry. What was it you ordered?

options.indonesian: Nasi goreng ayam satu, yang tidak pedas.
options.english: One chicken fried rice, not spicy.
options.feedback: Short and clear, the way orders are said: the dish, the number, and yang tidak pedas.
Fine for a new order, but it sounds like you're ordering again. Tadi saya pesan … (I ordered …) makes clear it's the order you've already placed.

options.indonesian: Saya sudah bilang tadi! Nasi goreng!
options.english: I already told you! Fried rice!
options.feedback: Snapping embarrasses everyone and won't get your food any faster. Calmly repeat the order.

n3.speaker: server
n3.indonesian: Baik, Kak, saya ganti, ya. Mohon ditunggu sebentar.
n3.english: Right, I'll change it. Please wait a moment.

options.feedback: Friendly, and it lets her off the hook. Nggak is fine with young staff in a relaxed café.
That turns down her offer to change it. She's bringing the right dish, so just say Iya, terima kasih.

n4.speaker: server
n4.indonesian: Bagaimana, Kak, nasi gorengnya? Sudah sesuai?
n4.english: How's the fried rice? Is it right this time?

options.feedback: Polite and specific: tadi points back to when you ordered, and yang tidak pedas is 'the not-spicy one'.

options.indonesian: Aduh, maaf, Mbak, ini masih pedas sekali buat saya.
options.english: Oh, sorry, it's still really spicy for me.
options.feedback: Aduh and maaf soften it, and buat saya (for me) makes it about your taste, not her mistake.

options.english: This is too hot (to the touch).
options.feedback: Panas is hot to the touch. Chilli hot is pedas: Ini terlalu pedas.

n5.speaker: server
n5.indonesian: Aduh, maaf sekali, Kak. Mau dibuatkan lagi, atau ganti menu lain?
n5.english: Oh, I'm so sorry. Shall we make it again, or would you like something else?

options.indonesian: Dibuatkan lagi saja, Mbak, tapi tidak pakai cabai sama sekali, ya.
options.english: Just make it again, please, but with no chilli at all.
options.feedback: Clear and friendly: tidak pakai cabai (no chilli) leaves the kitchen no room for 'just a little'.

options.indonesian: Ganti soto ayam saja, Mbak. Itu tidak pedas, kan?
options.english: I'll have the chicken soup instead. That's not spicy, is it?
options.feedback: Changing dish is fine too, and kan (isn't it?) checks before it comes.

options.indonesian: Saya tidak mau bayar untuk ini.
options.feedback: Confrontational when she's trying to fix it. Sort out the food first; you can check the bill at the end.

n6.speaker: server
n6.indonesian: Ini, Kak. Sekali lagi mohon maaf, ya. Es tehnya gratis.
n6.english: Here you are. Sorry again. The iced tea's on us.

options.feedback: Ending on thanks leaves everyone on good terms, and she keeps face.

options.indonesian: Wah, terima kasih, Mbak. Ini enak sekali.
options.english: Oh, thank you. This is delicious.
options.feedback: Praise and thanks: a warm end to a bumpy lunch.
Rubbing it in makes her lose face. Once it's sorted, Tidak apa-apa and thanks are all that's needed.

end.speaker: narration
end.english: Sorted. Maaf to start, bukan for 'not my order', tadi saya pesan … to point back to what you asked for, pedas (not panas) for chilli hot, and thanks at the end: a calm complaint gets results, and nobody loses face.
